entries.text: notebook: updated Gorrak Vael

You spit the gag, drive your forehead into the grey cloak's jaw, and roar through the shutters with everything left in you: Dreg, the book is behind the bedchamber door, break the stair, don't let them hang Gorrak. For one clear breath you hear the yard answer, spears on stone and Dreg's cadence-bellow rising over the bell.

The grey cloak's blade answers you first. The flat of it comes round, fast, and the world goes out. The last thing you see is Tessa's hand sliding a hairpin into the lock at her wrist.

You hear pieces of what follows, like a man under water. A door hammered in. A sergeant's voice. Tessa's hands on your chest, small and cold, and her voice in Draconic: "Breathe, Kor. Breathe. I have you."

You come up slowly, four hours later, with a thin winter sun in the shutter slats. It is a little before ten in the morning. You are on a pallet in the ledger-house's outer room with one hit point and your wrists bare, red and raw where the iron was cut off. Across your knees lies Dargan's greataxe with the ember-red sash tied to the haft.

Gorrak Vael crouches beside you, unmasked, the burn seam pale along his jaw and a rope-bruise purple round his neck. He looks like a man who has been hanged and cut down in the same minute. "Dreg's twenty took the stair, and the sentries on the gate-top threw down their spears when the boy Brun did. We lost three. The Foreman lost nine." He nods at the axe. "I said at the stones that I would give it back. I keep that kind of promise when I can."

Dreg stands at the door with a dozen Tallies, gruff and watchful. Krell sits against the wall with his arm in a sling, grinning crookedly.

Gorrak jerks his chin at the narrow door across the room. It's barred from within, and a line of lamplight shows beneath it. "He is in there with his book, four grey cloaks, and your sister. He says that if a spear comes through that door, Tessa dies first and the book burns second, and he means the first." A dry breath. "He wants you, Emberhide. He will talk to nobody else, and he says he has a new contract."

The room is quiet. Every Tally in it is looking at you, waiting to see what the man who read their captain's page aloud will do next.

You are at 1 hit point, with your father's axe across your knees. What does Korvash do?

sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. entries.text: notebook: updated Gorrak Vael

You whip your head back and spit the gag clear, and you drive your forehead into the grey cloak at your shoulder. Then you roar at the shutters, with Dreg and the book and Gorrak's neck in it. Across the room Tessa's hand goes up to her hair.

It is the last thing you do. The cloak you butted was the quickest man in the room. His pommel comes round with all of him behind it and finds the side of your skull, and the blow is a crit. You'd have died of it at any other time. These men were told to bring you back alive, so the pommel is turned and the dark is a clean one. The last thing you see is Tessa with a hairpin in her teeth and a cuff on her wrist that will not give. The hairpin skates, and the lock holds.

You wake slowly, on cold flagstones, to quiet. Your head throbs like a drum, and the wire is gone from your wrists. Someone has cut the cuffs off. It is a little before nine in the morning, three hours later, and you have 1 hit point.

The ledger-house is wrecked. The door hangs off one hinge, the table is on its side, and there is blood in the doorway and a dead grey cloak in the corner. Through the broken door comes pale morning light and the sound of men moving. They are Tallies, red and tin cloaks, with their spears grounded on the gate-top walk. Dreg's voice is giving orders. The gate beam stands empty over the yard, with its rope hanging slack.

Tessa kneels beside you with her wrist bandaged and the pin still in her hand. "Dreg broke the stair," she says, low and fast. "The grey cloaks fought on the walk and lost. Gorrak is up. They cut him down from the beam's edge before the rope was on." She jerks her chin at the narrow door at the back of the room. It is barred, and a heavy chest has been dragged against it from the other side, scraping the stone. "The Foreman's behind that, with four of his own and the book. He won't open. Dreg wants to fire the room, and Gorrak won't have it. He says the book must be read before it burns."

Her eyes are on you. "They're waiting for you, Kor. Gorrak said so. He wants to know what you'd do."

You are alive and unchained, at 1 hit point, with no weapon, no armor, and a mountain full of hobgoblins who have just decided which of them to follow. What does Korvash do?

entries.text: notebook: updated Skarn
18 meets AC 18, so it hits.

The axe slips from your fingers, and your boot-toe flicks it up into both hands before the ring of bows has quite understood. Then you are running, with the rage roaring in your ears and the frozen turf drumming under you. The grey cloaks have waited three nights for a beaten man to kneel. They are surprised, and for the length of one heartbeat nobody on the shelf moves but you.

Skarn's mouth is still open on the order when the greataxe comes round. The blade takes him under the arm and across the ribs, and he is flung from the Tally boy like a sack off a cart. The knife spins away into the dark. He is dead before he lands. The bound hobgoblin sprawls free on the turf, wide-eyed, and you plant a boot between him and the bows and shout in Goblin: "Down, lad! Roll away from the edge!"

Seven of the grey cloaks drop their weapons the moment their sergeant falls. Crossbows clatter on the frost, and hands go open and high. Four do not. Four bolts leave the bows in a ragged line. One whines past your ear, one misses, and two bite into your shoulder and side. The rage turns most of the sting into a deep bruise, and you stay on your feet. You are bloodied, though. You are at 17 of your 23 hit points. (Out of character: the first volley's damage was recorded at full by mistake, so I've corrected it for rage resistance.)

Now it is your turn again. Four grey cloaks stand with crossbows in the lee of the cut, ten or twelve paces off, already hauling at the strings. Seven more stand with their hands up. The bound Tally lies at your heel. The cairn is behind you, untouched. Your rage is burning, and your breath weapon still waits, a cone of fire that could take all four bowmen at once if they stand close.

What does Korvash do?

sheet.name: Korvash Emberhide
sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. line:
I raise my fist to the slab crews and keep it raised, whispering to Gorrak, "Hold until the file is strung out on the narrow, and not before." I tell Dreg to send two spears to meet the four heading for the Weeping Ledge, quietly, since they'll find it empty and then try to flank us.

When the first torch reaches the tight bend, I drop my fist and roar, "Slabs, now! Slingers, loose!", then step into the road with shield up beside Gorrak to hold the head of the column.
